source_evidence.finding: Casa Rosada defines the official national flag as three horizontal bands, two sky-blue and a white middle, with the sun reproduced in the middle from early Argentine gold and silver coins; it specifies the sun's golden-yellow colour.
The Interior Ministry page says the Inca sun was incorporated in the central white band on 25 February 1818 and identifies the 2010 decree that defines flag materials, colours, and accessories.

articles.factual_and_pedagogical_assessment: The article accurately describes the official national design with the central Sun of May and treats a plain sky-blue/white rendering only as a visually similar composition, without claiming that it is an equivalent official national design.

source_evidence.finding: Decreto Supremo 1534 states the two equal-height horizontal halves; the lower is red, while the upper is a blue third at the hoist and the remaining two thirds white, with a white five-point star centered in the blue square. It also says the blue square is upper left to the viewer for horizontal or vertical display only when it is not possible to fly the flag on a staff or mast.
Chile's Foreign Ministry identifies the current flag as a national emblem and dates its legalisation to 18 October 1817, with its first public use on 12 February 1818.

articles.factual_and_pedagogical_assessment: Initial review found that the orientation paragraph omitted the Article 3 condition. The final text now explicitly confines this placement rule to fully extended horizontal or vertical display when a staff or mast is unavailable; the corrected claim and the geometry, colours, star, and hoist-side description are accurate.
